_what_this_is: The batch manifest. CHAT WRITES THE IDS AND THEY ARE IMMUTABLE; the agent may only move `status` and add `evidence`. `id_lock` is a hash over the ordered id list and `batch_manifest.py --check` refuses a manifest whose ids have been renumbered, duplicated, added to or removed.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG: (F1, HIGH) addChargeEntry() has stamped cdt_code and cdt_version onto every charge since 2026-09-17 and its own comment states the guarantee -- 'the code and the edition are STAMPED AT POSTING' -- and BOTH READERS IGNORED THE STAMP: the patient ledger charges table at the old :5080 and the charges export's 'Procedure' column at the old :2106 both looked the code up LIVE from the mutable procedure-type row. The write half shipped, the read half did not, and nothing could tell because stamp and lookup agree on every row until the catalogue is edited -- the one day the stamp exists for. The export's own comment NINE LINES ABOVE the column it fixes states the rule it then broke. (F2) THE VERSIONING HAD NO WAY IN: the form was ADD-ONLY and the table's only action was Remove, so every row predating the feature reported 'Not verifiable' permanently with no path to a checked state, and applying a new CDT edition meant Remove-and-re-Add, which mints a new row id and orphans every historical charge. The 2026-09-17 stamping fix was written for an edit path that did not exist. FIXED: dntChargeCode() reads the stamp, falls back to the live row ONLY when there is no stamp and LABELS that ('as the catalogue reads today -- not stamped at posting'), and says 'not recorded' when neither exists rather than guessing; three new export columns (CDT code as billed, CDT edition as billed, Code source). startProcedureRevise()/cancelProcedureRevise() plus update-or-insert in addProcedureType(): same row id so posted charges stay attributable, replaced values APPENDED to revisions[] rather than overwritten, only changed fields recorded, and refusals for no-change, vanished-target and inverted-window.
